message: Greeting from Equipo Blinky; the presenter introduces himself: Andrés Leonardo Becerra López, AI Engineer; we came for the Blinka Task and the challenge turned out to be the Radar de Contenido of 30X, so we built a radar.

visual: chain diagram lighting up step by step
message: 30X's problem: paid scraping costs thousands a year and answers half the question. The insight: AI topics do not originate on LinkedIn; they travel down an open chain (papers, GitHub, Hacker News, X; then news in GDELT; then search and Wikipedia, Spanish later than English; only then LinkedIn and Instagram). A radar that watches the upstream layers and measures how far each topic travelled says what is ABOUT to land on LinkedIn, not what landed last week. LinkedIn is never scraped; only 30X's own analytics.

GDELT: open data that monitors the world's news; its knowledge graph extracts entities, themes and the TONE of every article; it updates every 15 minutes in 65 languages; here 4,031,651 AI-related articles over 51 weeks, 1,623,903 in the AI ring, processed in BigQuery for 0 dollars inside the free tier. Its value: tone per article, co-mentions between topics, and timing per language (when a topic explodes in English and has not reached Spanish).

The app live. Despegando is the top 10 of AI topics rising faster than their own history (W42 #1 Alianzas y adquisiciones en IA). One click opens the card: emergence, stage, the window (estimated days until it lands in Spanish), the emotional angle, and a decision computed by code. The Historia lens draws the topic's one-hop ring: its strongest neighbours that week, the articles that back it, so you see what the topic connects to.
Next to it, Lo más grande: the giants of the week by volume: Nvidia 4,718 articles, OpenAI 2,691, Microsoft, Google, Anthropic. Rising versus biggest: two different questions.

visual: clip 04_play slowed, then 05_lenses Radar and Familia
message: The graph plays 13 weeks: 105 AI topics connected by co-mentions weighted by NPMI. Size is importance (PageRank), colour the family; Leiden finds 7 communities. This is how the radar traces how news connects, week by week.

visual: clip 05_lenses Postura, Emocion, Momento, Puente, Novedad
message: Each lens answers a question for the content team: Emoción reads the tone GDELT measures in each article; Postura separates promoters from critics; Momento shows acceleration; Puente the bridges between sectors; Novedad the new links. The radar turns that tone into the framing angle: alerta, oportunidad, debate, giro or explicador; that is WHAT to publish and FROM WHICH PERSPECTIVE to gain followers.

And you can ask. The Media Master coordinates 8 agents: code writes the facts, the model explains them and an Auditor checks every number; in our evaluation, grounding 0.964. Asked what is biggest this week, it answers with the leaders, the why and what to do.
And it is honest about trust: the backtest says the ranking is relevant but not yet better than chance on its labels; it is an early signal, not a guarantee.

It is built to be implemented: deployed on Cloud Run and Netlify, CI on every pull request, 130 of 130 browser checks passing, traces in LangSmith, secrets in Secret Manager. Cost: BigQuery inside the free tier, about 13 dollars a month of server, a tenth of a cent per chat answer, versus thousands a year in scraping.

visual: avatar closing with name and LinkedIn
message: The ask: a 4-week pilot with 30X's media team; they read the weekly radar and share their own post analytics, so the radar learns what works for their followers. Closing: Radar de Señal Temprana, Equipo Blinky; the presenter's name and that the LinkedIn and the live app are on screen.
